item.title: Things to Do in NYC This Week (July 27 - Aug 2)
item.description: Line dancing, grocery store theater, and ThriftCon
item.dc:creator: Alexa Weiser
item.content:encoded:
A friend recently came back from a Europe trip and was telling me about all the museums, walking tours, and shows they squeezed into a few days. It struck me that when we travel, we’re eager to understand a place, know its history, and generally just experience more than the highlights. Then we come home and we stop doing that.

This weekend I went on a walking tour of the West Village, a neighborhood I actually used to live in. I expected to hear a few fun facts I’d probably already know. Instead, I realized how little I actually understood about the streets I’d walked hundreds of times. Every few blocks there was another story about a building, a person, or some small piece of New York history I’d completely missed. Most of them even had plaques I'd somehow never noticed, but now feel impossible to miss. By the end, I’d opened about fifteen tabs on my phone because I wanted to keep reading.

I think a lot of us have an instinct to avoid looking like tourists in our own city. In New York especially, there's almost a badge of honor in acting like you've seen it all already. But I think we're missing out because of it.

I'm not suggesting you suddenly start walking half the speed of everyone else or that you stop reading on the subway to stare out the window. But every once in a while, it’s worth doing something designed to help you understand the city rather than simply move through it. I left the tour with a renewed appreciation for a neighborhood I thought I already knew.

Monday July 27

⭐ Jake Cohen & Friends
Underground Overground | 8:30pm at 251 Montrose Ave, East Williamsburg

New York Times bestselling cookbook author and dinner-party king Jake Cohen is trading the kitchen for the comedy stage, hosting a one-night show with some of his favorite comedians inside Underground Overground’s Brooklyn warehouse. It’ll be an evening with some of his favorite comedians alongside light bites, desserts, and drinks included with admission. Tickets are $70.

Subscribe for the best things to do in NYC.

Soho Diner Backgammon Night
NYC Backgammon Club | 7-10pm at 320 W Broadway, Soho

NYC Backgammon Club is taking over Soho Diner for an evening of casual games, happy hour, and meeting fellow backgammon players. The club is still one of my favorite social groups and draws everyone from complete beginners to longtime players at their events. Bring your own board if you have one, or just come to learn. Tickets are $10.

Seashell Trinket Dish Craft Night
Chaotic Good Cafe | 7-9pm at 200 W 84th St, Upper West Side

Craft Club NYC is teaming up with WP Theater for a summery craft night where you’ll decorate seashell trinket dishes using vintage William Morris-inspired patterns. No experience is needed and all supplies are included. Tickets are $30, and you can use code CRAFTY for $10 off tickets to The Betrothed, the Off-Broadway comedy that inspired the event.

Tuesday July 28

Artists at Work: Chris Zhongtian Yuan in Conversation with Jeff Preiss
ISCP | 6:30-7:30pm at 1040 Metropolitan Ave, East Williamsburg

London-based artist Chris Zhongtian Yuan joins filmmaker Jeff Preiss for a conversation at the International Studio & Curatorial Program about experimental filmmaking, installation art, and the creative communities that have influenced their work across New York and beyond. The discussion will be followed by an audience Q&A, and visitors can also explore ISCP's current exhibitions before or after the program. Free to attend, see event details for more info.

Line Dancing at Roberta’s
Rogers Rodeo | 7-10pm at 261 Moore St, East Williamsburg

One of the city’s liveliest recurring line dancing nights returns to Roberta’s for an evening of two-stepping, pizza, and drinks. A beginner lesson kicks things off from 7-8pm before the dance floor opens up for intermediate and advanced dances, all led by DJ Gold Rush of Rogers Rodeo. RSVP for free.

Wednesday July 29

⭐ Little Island Summer Shows
Little Island | July 29-Aug 16 at Pier 55, Hudson River Park

Every summer Little Island fills its amphitheater with an eclectic lineup of concerts, theater, dance, comedy, and one-night-only collaborations that are far more ambitious than you’d expect from a public park. The 2026 season kicks off tonight with cabaret icon Justin Vivian Bond’s Summer’s Eve, followed by performances from Louis Cato, Cécile McLorin Salvant, Julio Torres, Anthony Roth Costanzo, and more throughout the summer. Tickets start at just $15 and many sell out fast. Check out the full lineup.

Will Run for Wine 5K
On Cloud Wine | 7-10pm at 462 Union Ave, Williamsburg

If your ideal reward for finishing a run is a glass of wine, this one’s for you. On Cloud Wine and Queer Feet are hosting a social 5K through Williamsburg followed by an afterparty at Rude Mouth, where your registration includes a welcome pour. If your goal is to PR, then this may not be for you. Tickets are $28.

Thursday July 30

⭐ Have the Ivies Failed America?
UNMUTED | 6:30-8:30pm at 12-16 Vestry St, Tribeca

UNMUTED hosts debates designed for people who actually enjoy hearing both sides of an argument. Their latest tackles a provocative question: Have the Ivy League schools failed America? Columbia graduate and finance professional Mark Carlson argues that the institutions have lost their way, while Harvard and Yale alum Victor Agbafe makes the case for why they still deserve their outsized influence. The evening includes audience discussion and drinks. Tickets are $30.

Salsa Under the Stars II
Lehman Center | 6-9pm at 250 Bedford Park Blvd W, Bronx

One of the Bronx’s biggest outdoor salsa parties returns this week with live music from Tres Del Solar and DJ Woody keeping the dance floor going all evening. Presented with The Salsa Project, the night pairs social dancing with food and drinks from Havana Café, making it just as welcoming for people who want to listen and soak up the atmosphere as those ready to dance. RSVP for free.

Big Apple Roll
Big Apple Roll | July 30-Aug 2 at various locations throughout the city

More than 1,000 rollerbladers from around the world are expected to take over New York for Big Apple Roll, a four-day celebration of skating through the city. Organized by the Empire Skate Club, the annual weekend features group skates past iconic landmarks, social events, and parties. Even if you’re not lacing up your own skates, it’s worth keeping an eye out for the massive packs rolling through the streets. They have a party to cap it all off on Saturday night too. Check out the full schedule of events.

Shelf Life
Horseradish Market | 9:15pm at 867 Broadway, Bushwick

When Horseradish Market closes for the night, it transforms into an immersive theater experience where the grocery store comes to life. Guided by the ghost of an extinct banana, you’ll wander through a surreal world of live music, clowning, comedy, and talking produce. Probably the most Bushwick thing I’ve ever heard of. Tickets are $15, and City Happenings readers can use code SHELFLIFE1 for $5 off.

Friday July 31

Eavesdropping: The Erotics of Listening
The Lighthouse | 8pm at 603 Bergen St, Prospect Park

One of the more unusual talks I’ve come across lately asks a surprisingly interesting question: why are conversations we’re not supposed to hear often the most interesting? Composer and artist Whitney George explores the strange psychology of eavesdropping through film, opera, sound art, and everyday life in what’s part lecture, part listening session, and part group discussion. Tickets are $30.

Poetry and Place
The Met | 6-7pm at 1000 Fifth Avenue, Upper East Side

The Met is hosting an evening of original poetry and live oud music inside its Ancient West Asian galleries. The performances, created by this year’s Narratio Fellows, draw inspiration from objects in the museum’s collection while exploring themes of memory, migration, identity, and belonging. I always like when museums find ways to activate their galleries beyond traditional tours and this one feels thoughtful and fun. Free with museum admission.

Saturday Aug 1

FAD Market at The Seaport
FAD Market | 11am-6pm at 89 South St, Fidi

One of my favorite maker markets returns to the Seaport this weekend. FAD Market is bringing together more than 50 independent artists and designers selling handcrafted jewelry, ceramics, apparel, home goods, and other small-batch finds. The waterfront setting makes it an especially great way to spend a summer afternoon. Free with no RSVP needed.

⭐ ThriftCon NYC
Brooklyn Storehouse | 10am-6pm at 35 Meadow St, East Williamsburg

If you love thrifting, this is one of the biggest events of the year. ThriftCon brings together more than 100 carefully curated vintage dealers from around the country selling everything from archival designer pieces and graphic tees to Y2K fashion, collectibles, furniture, and home goods. Beyond the shopping, there are live performances, special activations, and a dedicated “Vault” showcasing some of the country’s top vintage T-shirt collectors. Tickets start at $39.

⭐ Summer Streets: Manhattan
Summer Streets | 7am-3pm from the Brooklyn Bridge to Inwood

There’s something especially magical about Summer Streets in Manhattan. For one morning, Park Avenue, Lafayette Street, and Broadway transform into a nearly 13-mile car-free route stretching from the Brooklyn Bridge all the way to Inwood. Whether you bike the full length, walk a section you’ve never explored, or simply stop to enjoy the pop-up performances, fitness classes, art installations, and rest stops along the way, it’s one of those days that completely changes how the city feels. Last year I ran part of it, and the rush of adrenaline and appreciation I felt for living in New York has been hard to replicate. See the full schedule of summer streets throughout the boroughs if you can’t make this one.

Su’juk Turns 14
Su’juk | 3-8pm at 216 Greene Ave, Clinton Hill

One of Brooklyn’s most beloved neighborhood stores is celebrating 14 years with an afternoon block party. Stop by for DJs, special drinks from Golden Ratio, and portraits by film photographer Montana Ray, Su’juk’s very first customer. If you’re in the neighborhood, go drink and dance with them!

Sunday Aug 2

Lunch with Joe Beddia
Smithereens | From 12-3pm at 414 E 9th St, East Village

Smithereens is kicking off a new lunch series inviting chefs and wine experts to help shape a one-day-only menu, and the first guest is legendary Philadelphia pizza maker Joe Beddia. You’ll be served an Italian-American-inspired prix fixe lunch featuring boardwalk favorites like fried scallops and potatoes, paired with a welcome pour and a wine list curated by Beddia himself. The prix-fixe menu is $65.

Symmetry and the City: A Walk with Chaim Goodman-Strauss
Museum of Mathematics | 9:30-10:30am at 635 Sixth Ave, Flatiron

You’ll never look at New York buildings quite the same way after this walking tour led by mathematician and geometer Chaim Goodman-Strauss. Beginning at the Museum of Mathematics, the hour-long walk explores the hidden patterns, symmetries, and geometric details woven into 19th-century architecture, from tiled façades to carved windowsills. Tickets are $30.

What I did last week.

Places or shows I went to over the last week. These are personal recommendations. If I had a cool week, they’ll be cool. If I didn’t, they won’t.

  1. Literary Pub Crawl - I went on what ended up being a mix between a city walking tour and a pub crawl through the West Village. Despite the name, we learned about far more than literary history, touching on architecture, the evolution of Manhattan, and the stories behind so many buildings and streets I walk past all the time. Our guide was shockingly knowledgeable, and it was a fun way to feel like a tourist in your own city.

  2. Bridges - I understand why Bridges has a Michelin star. We went with a group and ordered almost the entire menu, and there wasn't a single dish I wouldn't happily order again. It's definitely fish-forward, but we ended up eating just as many non-seafood dishes as seafood ones. Also worth noting: they make an excellent espresso martini.

  3. All’antico Vinaio - There’s no better way to spend a sunny afternoon in New York, than picking up a picnic and finding a spot in the park. That’s exactly what I did with one of All’Antico Vinaio’s enormous focaccia sandwiches. It was delicious and honestly so big that it ended up being both lunch and dinner.

  4. Jimmy - I ended up here for a work happy hour, and it's hard to beat the sunset views. I did almost fall into the pool trying to squeeze between people on the narrow walkway, but thankfully made it out dry.

  5. L’Americana - My friends and I were wandering around looking for somewhere to grab a drink and ended up taking the first open sidewalk table we could find. It turned out to be a great decision. L’Americana is an ideal happy hour spot, especially if you like people-watching. Sitting on the corner of a busy intersection, there’s always something happening. We stayed much longer than we’d planned just soaking it all in.

item.title: Things to Do in NYC This Week (July 20 - 26)
item.description: 12 horror authors, beach clam shacks & kung fu hip hop
item.dc:creator: Alexa Weiser
item.content:encoded:
This weekend I was in the Hamptons celebrating one of my oldest friends’ bachelorette. My favorite part wasn’t the beach or the dinners. It was getting to spend a few days with all the people who have shaped her life.

When I got married, I was actually nervous about this exact thing. I worried I’d spend the whole weekend bouncing between friend groups who didn’t know each other, trying to make sure everyone felt included. I guess as a type-A planner, I was mostly focused on the logistics.

But being on the other side of it is one of my favorite things. I got to understand my friend through everyone else. She also did something I hadn’t seen before and invited both of her siblings, including her brother. Having them there completely changed the energy of the weekend. I’ve known their family since we were kids, so getting to watch the three of them slip right back into their old rhythms of teasing each other and giggling over jokes from twenty years ago was really special. I suspect this might be one of my last, at least for a while. I'm both a little sad about that and kind of okay with it.

Monday July 20

Why Wine Is Beautiful: The Story Hidden in Every Bottle
Maison Sun | 6:30-8:30pm in the West Village (location shared after registration)

This isn’t a wine tasting or a lesson on tannins. Instead, restaurateur and former literature professor Carlos Gasperi explores wine through history, geography, and storytelling, examining how climate, culture, and generations of winemakers shape what’s in your glass. It’ll be an interactive conversation designed for curious drinkers, followed by time to ask questions and mingle over a glass of wine. Tickets are $30.

Subscribe for the best things to do in NYC.

Work in Good Company
Good Company | 6-8pm at 2273 Broadway, Upper West Side

, who writes the neighborhood newsletter The Upper West Insider, is hosting a creative coworking session for anyone with a project they’ve been meaning to finish. Bring your laptop, notebook, sketchbook, or half-written Substack draft, then spend the afternoon working alongside other writers, artists, founders, and creatives. The evening begins with casual introductions so you can share what you’re building and meet potential collaborators before settling in to work. Tickets are $20 and include a $5 credit to Good Company Shop.

Tuesday July 21

Casa Collage Club
Casa Next Door | 6:30-9pm at 181 8th Ave, West Village

Casa Next Door is having their monthly Casa Collage Club which pairs a small group with collage artist Francesca Maida for a workshop where you’ll learn a few techniques before creating your own piece. All materials are included and you’ll leave with a finished 9×12 collage plus a handmade collage kit. Tickets are $58.

⭐ Summer of Horrors
Brooklyn Brewery x The Twisted Spine | 5-8:30pm at 79 N 11th St, Williamsburg

Twelve horror writers are taking over Brooklyn Brewery for an evening of author panels, book signings, and all things spooky. The event marks the first stop of Christopher Golden’s unconventional Carry Me to My Grave book tour, which doubles as a pop-up horror convention featuring conversations with bestselling and award-winning authors including Victor LaValle, Nat Cassidy, Clay McLeod Chapman, and more. You can RSVP for free or grab a ticket that includes one of the 12 books of your choice, with opportunities to meet the authors and have books signed after the panels.

Wednesday July 22

⭐ ISCP Summer Celebration & Open House
ISCP | 5-9pm at 1040 Metropolitan Ave, East Williamsburg

The International Studio & Curatorial Program is opening its studios for one of its biggest public events of the year. More than two dozen artists and curators currently in residence will be presenting their work throughout the building, giving visitors the chance to explore studios, chat with artists, and see what an international residency program actually looks like behind the scenes. Two solo exhibitions will also be on view, including Bryan Fernandez’s En tránsito and Hans Rosenström’s Conspirare. Free, no RSVP required. Check out the full list of participating artists.

Herring Pairing
Russ & Daughters Cafe | 6pm at 127 Orchard St, Lower East Side

Russ & Daughters is returning to its roots with an evening dedicated to the fish that started it all. The cocktail-style tasting celebrates New Catch Holland Herring at the height of its season, with passed bites showcasing different preparations alongside drink pairings. The event also nods to the shop’s origins, which began over a century ago selling herring from a barrel on the Lower East Side. Come hungry and ready to mingle with fellow herring enthusiasts. Tickets are $125.

⭐ Matchbook Fest
Greenwich House Theater | Through Aug 22nd at 27 Barrow St, West Village

Greenwich House Theater, one of the city’s most beloved Off-Broadway venues, is spending five weeks handing its stage over to the next generation of theatermakers. Matchbook Fest brings together playwrights, composers, comedians, and performers to debut brand-new work, from first readings and experimental musicals to cabaret, comedy, and one-night-only performances. Rather than polished productions, many of these shows are being tested in front of audiences for the very first time, offering a chance to see ideas evolve before they make their way to larger stages. Tickets start at $40.

Thursday July 23

Summer Picnic Series
Poppy’s | Thursdays 5-7pm at 48 Henry St, Brooklyn Heights

One of Brooklyn’s best summer traditions now has a dinner option. Every Thursday, Poppy’s is staying open late with fried chicken picnic dinners timed to Brooklyn Bridge Park’s Movies With A View series. Grab your meal before heading to the waterfront for a free outdoor movie overlooking the Manhattan skyline. On July 23, they’ll be pairing the menu with The Talented Mr. Ripley. Pre-order ahead or stop by. The menu also includes mac n’ cheese, heirloom tomato & peach salad, and corn jalapeno buttermilk biscuits. Sounds better than the popcorn I usually bring.

Amigas Coffee Talk NYC
Saturn Road | 10-11:30am at 276 Court St, Cobble Hill

Amigas Means Friends is hosting a morning coffee conversation with Jen Frodsham, founder of Power Meets Presence, on navigating life transitions and building a life that feels more intentional. The gathering begins with a guided meditation before moving into a moderated conversation, audience discussion, and Q&A over coffee. Your ticket includes your first drink and is geared toward women looking for a thoughtful way to start the day. Tickets are $15.

The Space Between Tables: Third Culture Cooking and Belonging
Kitchen Arts & Letters | 6:30-8pm at 111 Broadway, Fidi

Four of today’s most compelling cookbook authors are coming together for a conversation about how migration, family, and identity shape the way we cook. Moderated by Eater’s Bettina Makalintal, the panel features Eric Kim, Zaynab Issa (Third Culture Cooking), Hawa Hassan (In Bibi’s Kitchen), and Stacey Mei Yan Fong (50 Pies, 50 States) discussing everything from reinventing childhood dishes to preserving family traditions. Stick around afterward for a book signing. Tickets are $15.

Friday July 24

Kung Fu Hip Hop
Lincoln Center | 6pm at 10 Lincoln Center Plaza, Upper West Side

As part of Lincoln Center’s Chinese Arts Week, hip-hop crews and martial artists come together for a performance exploring the longtime overlap between breaking, popping, locking, and kung fu. There will be high-energy dance battles, acrobatics, and performers blending traditional Chinese dress with contemporary streetwear in a showcase that’s a mix of dance performance and martial arts exhibition. Free. First come, first served.

⭐ Rolo’s Clam Shack
Brothers Rockaway | 5-8:30pm at 106-01 Shore Front Pkwy, Rockaway Beach

For one night only, Ridgewood favorite Rolo’s is heading to the beach. The restaurant is popping up at Brothers Rockaway as “Rolo’s Clam Shack”, serving a summery menu of fried local clams, lobster rolls, ceviche, peach panzanella, and other seafood specials right on the boardwalk. It’s first come, first served, so I’d expect a line. RSVP for free.

Bugging Out at Night!
Green-Wood Cemetery | 8:30-10pm at 500 25th St, Greenwood Heights

Green-Wood is opening its gates after sunset for a look at the wildlife that emerges once the cemetery quiets down. Using ultraviolet lights, naturalists will attract moths, often called the “jewels of the night,” along with beetles, katydids, ants, and other nocturnal insects that most visitors never get to see. It’s part nature walk, part nighttime safari, part my worst nightmare. Tickets are $25.

Saturday July 25

All-White Rooftop Fundraiser
Unlisted Rooftop x startswithus | 3-7pm at 3 Freeman Alley, Lower East Side

Community group startswithus is taking over Unlisted Rooftop for an all-white summer fundraiser featuring music from DJ Dilly Rowe. Founded around the idea that community starts with showing up, startswithus organizes low-barrier volunteer experiences and social events that help young New Yorkers connect with both each other and local nonprofits. It will be an afternoon of rooftop drinks, dancing, and meeting new people, with proceeds supporting the organization’s volunteer programming and community events across the city. Tickets are $25.

Pasta Class at Casa Rina
LaRina Pastificio & Vino | 12-3:30pm at 387 Myrtle Ave, Fort Greene

Chef Silvia Barban is hosting an afternoon of pasta making, aperitivos, and a long Italian lunch at Casa Rina. The hands-on class is followed by a live cooking demonstration, then a family-style meal featuring the pasta you’ve made alongside seasonal dishes, tiramisù, and wine served throughout. Tickets are $150.

WILLOW Album Signing
Vinyl + Thread | 5:30pm at 55 Anchorage Pl., Dumbo

WILLOW is celebrating the release of her new album The Thread with a photo meet-and-greet at Vinyl + Thread, Brooklyn’s new record store and vintage shop from the founders of the beloved Canal Room. Your ticket includes a signed copy of the album on limited-edition neon magenta cloud vinyl, plus a chance to meet the artist and snap a photo. Tickets are $55.

⭐ Brooklyn Tides: Excerpts from New York Waterfront Diary
Gowanus Dredgers Boathouse | 1-5pm at 165 2nd St, Gowanus

Photographer Sophie Fenwick is exhibiting three decades of Brooklyn waterfront photography, tracing neighborhoods like Gowanus, Red Hook, Sunset Park, Dumbo, and the Navy Yard from the 1990s through the years before the pandemic. For City of Water Day, the exhibition expands beyond still images with a screening of Fenwick’s Super 8 footage from the early ‘90s, accompanied by live music from Leslie Braver. The Gowanus Dredgers will also be offering free walk-up paddling throughout the afternoon. Check out the exhibition details, no RSVP needed.

Sunday July 26

⭐ Brooklyn Summer Market
Markets for Makers | Sat & Sun 11am-5pm at 33 35th St, Sunset Park

One of the country’s largest curated maker markets returns to Industry City with more than 90 artists, designers, and small businesses selling everything from ceramics and jewelry to home goods, clothing, candles, and specialty foods. Beyond the shopping, there are free DIY craft stations, themed photo installations, and plenty of food vendors throughout the day. It’s one of the better markets for discovering independent brands at reasonable prices. Tickets start at $8.

Morning Tea & Bagels in the Park
Unfurl Tea Community | 10am-12pm in Central Park (exact location shared after registration)

Tea community Unfurl is hosting a slow Sunday morning built around cold brew tea, New York bagels, and unhurried conversation in Central Park. The picnic includes a bagel bar, three varieties of iced tea, and tea-themed conversation prompts designed to help strangers get talking without forcing awkward icebreakers. It’ll be a small group of fellow tea enthusiasts looking to spend a couple of hours outside. Tickets are $15.

Natural Bee Workshop
Museum of Reclaimed Urban Space | 3-4pm at 9th St & Avenue C, East Village

The Museum of Reclaimed Urban Space is bringing Rutgers entomology researchers to La Plaza Community Garden for an afternoon dedicated to New York’s native bees. You’ll learn how to identify different bee species, why they’re essential to the city’s ecosystem, and how community gardens like this one help support urban pollinators. RSVP for free.

What I did last week.

Places or shows I went to over the last week. These are personal recommendations. If I had a cool week, they’ll be cool. If I didn’t, they won’t.

  1. Death Ave Wines - It feels like every wine shop these days wants to be more than a wine shop. At minimum they’re hosting tastings. Death Ave Wines actually succeeds at becoming somewhere you want to linger. The dimly lit space, highly curated selection, and musky incense make it feel more like a perfume boutique than a bottle shop. I stopped in to grab a gift for a friend and ended up chatting with one of the staff for almost 20 minutes.

  2. Barbuto - My first time at Barbuto’s location beneath 1 Hotel Brooklyn Bridge. I was there for an intimate rehearsal dinner, which felt perfectly suited to the space. The windows were thrown open, the evening light poured in, and dishes just kept arriving family-style. It struck me as an ideal spot for a gathering like a birthday dinner.

  3. Gertie - I’d obviously been to Gertie before given it’s one of my neighborhood staples. This recommendation is specifically for The Best Bialy sandwich, which I somehow ended up ordering three mornings in a row. I’m usually not a smoked salmon schmear person, but this completely changed my mind. It also remains one of my favorite patios in Prospect Heights.

  4. Ursula - The best breakfast burrito in the city. I’ll fight you on it.

item.title: Things to Do in NYC This Week (July 13 - 19)
item.description: A New York City Wedding Is Incredibly Chic
item.dc:creator: Alexa Weiser
item.content:encoded:
This weekend I went to my first-ever New York City wedding. Oddly, despite most of my friends living here, I’d never been to one before. Even my friends who grew up in New York usually end up getting married somewhere else.

I spend so much time talking about New York as a place to discover new restaurants, museums, neighborhoods, and events, but it's most importantly the backdrop to so many people's actual lives. Watching two friends get married overlooking Brooklyn Bridge Park, a place that's woven into their everyday routine, made me appreciate the city in a different way.

I'm still coming off that high. It also happened to be one of my busiest weeks in a while. Between exploring for the newsletter and finding excuses to stay out of my apartment while the cockroach situation resolves itself, I said yes to a few too many things. Tonight's plan is much less ambitious: a long walk through Prospect Park with my dog and a massage at my favorite no-frills neighborhood spot.

Monday July 13

⭐ Mahjong Night
Yingtao | 6-10pm at 805 9th Ave., Hell’s Kitchen

Mahjong nights continue to have their moment. Yingtao is partnering with hospitality collective After Eden for an evening of cocktails, small bites, mahjong, and board games designed to bring together restaurant industry folks, creatives, and anyone looking to meet new people. Your ticket includes a signature cocktail, a selection of Yingtao snacks, and access to games throughout the night. Mahjong tables are first come, first served. Tickets are $65.

Subscribe for the best things to do in NYC.

Connection Academy 101: Creating Belonging
week nights | 6:30-8:30pm at 33 W 17th St, Flatiron

The people behind week nights are launching a workshop series on how to actually build community. This first session covers everything from clarifying what your community exists to do to designing gatherings people actually want to come back to. It’ll be a hands-on evening with discussions, exercises, and other aspiring community builders. Plus you’ll get access to your cohort community WhatsApp group so you can keep trading notes. RSVP for free.

Tuesday July 14

Bryant Park Poetry Series
Reading Room | 6-7:15pm at Bryant Park

Bryant Park’s long-running summer poetry series continues with an evening of readings from Pulitzer Prize winner Philip Schultz alongside J Brooke, Nicole Santalucia, and R.A. Villanueva. The weekly series pairs established and emerging poets in the park’s Reading Room, making it one of the easiest ways to hear great contemporary poetry outdoors in the middle of Midtown. Free with no RSVP needed. See the full summer lineup for future readings.

Ice Cream Sundae Pop-Up
Candor x Cool Stuff | 6-8pm at 664 Fulton St, Fort Greene

I love when Substackers collaborate!!! Cat from and are teaming up with Alec’s Ice Cream for a one-night-only sundae pop-up featuring a matcha chocolate chip base topped with strawberry drizzle, strawberry gummies, and dipped pretzels. The sundae is free for Cool Stuff NYC subscribers and the team will be there scooping and hanging out throughout the evening.

Wednesday July 15

⭐ Morning Market Meetings with Suzanne Cupps
Union Square Cafe | 9-11am at 101 E 19th St, Union Square

One of Union Square Cafe’s best traditions is back. Their Morning Market Meetings series pairs breakfast with conversations featuring some of New York’s most influential chefs, followed by a guided walk through the Union Square Greenmarket. This month’s guest is Suzanne Cupps of Lola’s, whose seasonal cooking is deeply shaped by the market and its farmers. Your ticket includes pastries, coffee, tea, the conversation moderated by Executive Chef Lena Ciardullo, and a Greenmarket stroll with a curated shopping list inspired by the discussion. Tickets are $85.

Higher Fitness Series
Superfly Dispensary | July 15-17 at 57 W 86th St, Upper West Side

Cannabis dispensary Superfly is teaming up with wellness community High Ambitions for a three-day morning fitness series on the Upper West Side. Each day focuses on a different class (yoga on Tuesday, Pilates sculpt on Wednesday, and self-defense on Thursday), with sessions designed to get you moving before work. All classes are free, open to all experience levels, and take place inside the dispensary. RSVP for free.

Backgammon Night
Pinky Swear | 6:30pm at 171A Chrystie St., Lower East Side

Pinky Swear is hosting its first-ever Backgammon Night with specialty cocktails, immersive art installations, music from Lord Fascinator, and both a competitive tournament and casual open play. The tournament has already sold out, but open play tickets are still available for all skill levels if you’re looking to learn, meet other players, or challenge friends over a drink. BYO backgammon board if you have one. Tickets are $12.

Thursday July 16

⭐ Jazz in July
Brooklyn Botanic Garden | 6-8pm at 990 Washington Ave, Prospect Heights

Truly one of the best ways to spend a summer evening. Spread out on the Garden lawn with a blanket and settle in for an evening of live jazz, presented in partnership with local arts organizations. Performances begin at 7pm, with each night also featuring a Garden tour or other activity before the music starts. If you can’t make it this week, there’s another show on the 23rd. A pop-up bar will be on site for food & drinks too. Free with Garden admission.

GonzoFest NYC
GonzoFest | July 16-19 across the city

For ten years, GonzoFest celebrated the life and legacy of Hunter S. Thompson in Louisville. This year it’s coming to New York for the first time with four days of free panels, poetry, live music, art exhibitions, walking tours, film screenings, and late-night events spread across venues like Joe’s Pub, Howl! Happening, The Bitter End, Book Club Bar, and more. There will be conversations on Thompson’s political writing, Beat Generation connections, New York years, and journalism alongside appearances from writers, artists, musicians, and Thompson collaborators. Most programming is free, with a handful of ticketed events. Check out the full schedule.

A Night at Niblo’s Garden
Green-Wood Cemetery | 7-9pm in Greenwood Heights

One of Green-Wood’s most beloved annual events returns, transforming the cemetery into a 19th-century pleasure garden inspired by the legendary Niblo’s Garden. It’ll be an evening of fire-eaters, musicians, dancers, contortionists, and circus performers by the Bindlestiff Family Cirkus around Crescent Water, plus access inside the Niblo mausoleum before the show begins. Tickets are $55.

⭐ Curator Talk: 50 Years of Stories
New York Transit Museum | 6-7:30pm at 99 Schermerhorn St, Downtown Brooklyn

The New York Transit Museum is celebrating its 50th anniversary with a special exhibition featuring artifacts and lesser-known moments from the city’s transit history. This curator-led talk goes behind the scenes of the exhibition, exploring how the team uncovered and connected stories spanning New York’s past, present, and future through its subway system. Tickets are $15.

Friday July 17

Mary Ross and Friends
Parkside Lounge | 6:30pm at 317 E Houston St., Lower East Side

Comedian and psychology PhD student Mary Ross hosts an evening where some of NYC’s best comedians and performers tell true, personal stories live on stage. It’s meant to be a mix of comedy, storytelling, and heartfelt moments in one of the Lower East Side’s classic dive bars. Tickets are $14 in advance.

¡Vamos! A Celebration of Latin and Caribbean Cultures
American Museum of Natural History | 7-10pm at 200 Central Park W, Upper West Side

The American Museum of Natural History is throwing an after-hours celebration of Latin and Caribbean cultures ahead of the World Cup Final. Expect DJ sets, samba performances, a pop-up market featuring local makers, dominoes tournaments, Spades lessons, talks with museum researchers, and an art installation exploring soccer as a universal language of migration and community. You’ll also have after-hours access to the museum, including its new sports exhibition For the Win: Objects of Sports Excellence. Tickets are $30 ($25 for members).

Jazz at the Plaza
Abrons Arts Center | 6–8pm at 466 Grand St, Lower East Side

Abrons Arts Center has been a Lower East Side arts institution for more than a century, presenting theater, dance, music, and visual art as part of the Henry Street Settlement. This Friday they're launching a new free summer jazz series with live performances in the outdoor plaza featuring Zacchae'us Paul and band. Bring a blanket or pull up a chair for an evening of music under the open sky. Register for free.

Saturday July 18

⭐ Brooklyn Pop-Up Summer Market [EDIT: THIS HAS BEEN MOVED TO NEXT WEEKEND]
Hook Studios | Sat & Sun at 12-6pm at 161 Dikeman St, Red Hook

If you need an excuse to spend an afternoon in Red Hook (you shouldn’t), this is a good one. More than 50 local artists, makers, and artisans will fill Hook Studios with ceramics, jewelry, home goods, art, vintage finds, and hands-on crafting activities. To make it the perfect day, stop by Strong Rope Brewery or Steve’s Key Lime Pie before heading home. The market is hosted by Brooklyn Pop-Up, the organization that hosts all the familiar favorite markets like the recurring ones at Fort Greene Park and the Brooklyn Museum so you know it’ll be good. Free to attend, no RSVP needed.

⭐ Harlem Walking Tour with John T. Reddick
Poster House | 11am-1pm in Harlem

Poster House is taking its excellent Act Black: Posters from Black American Stage & Screen exhibition into the streets of Harlem. Led by historian and architectural preservationist John T. Reddick, this walking tour visits landmarks like Strivers’ Row, the Schomburg Center, and Harlem Hospital while exploring how the neighborhood shaped Black performance, public life, and the Harlem Renaissance. Reddick has spent decades documenting Harlem’s history, making this one of those rare opportunities to experience the neighborhood through the eyes of someone who has helped preserve it. Tickets are $25.

Gestural Listening: Sound, Touch, and the Body
Pioneer Works | 2pm at 159 Pioneer Street, Red Hook

Pioneer Works is hosting a hands-on workshop exploring how movement can become music. Inspired by its current exhibition ANIMAL [a listening gym], participants will use sensors and simple electronics to turn gestures, touch, and body movement into sound. No musical or technical experience is required, and everyone leaves with their own electronics kit. Tickets are $85.

Sunday July 19

NYC Plant Market
Culture Lab LIC | 1-7pm at 5-25 46th Ave., Long Island City

The city’s biggest plant market of the year returns to Culture Lab LIC with dozens of plant vendors, including Annie’s Jungle Shop and Bonsai Bar, plus a community plant swap, a free plant clinic where you can get advice on your struggling houseplants, live music, local food vendors, beer and wine, and an art exhibition. Whether you’re looking for your next monstera or just want to spend a Sunday afternoon surrounded by fellow plant people, this is one to bookmark. Free admission, no RSVP needed.

⭐ Bark Bash
Friends & Lovers | 1-4pm at 641 Classon Ave., Crown Heights

Spend your Sunday meeting adoptable dogs while supporting a great cause. Bark Bash brings together Every Last One Rescue with tattoo artists, tarot readers, aura photography, permanent jewelry, raffles, vegetarian food, drinks, and other local vendors, all benefiting Animal Farm Foundation’s programs that help keep pets and families together. Whether you’re looking to adopt or just want to hang out with dogs for the afternoon, it’s a fun way to support NYC’s animal welfare community. Suggested donation at the door. No RSVP needed.

Bastille Day at L’Appartement 4F
L’Appartement 4F | 2pm at 115 Montague St., Brooklyn Heights

L’Appartement 4F is turning Montague Street into a French-inspired block party for Bastille Day in partnership with Brooklyn Heights Open Streets. There will be natural wine, beer, French cheeses and charcuterie, grilled small plates, peak summer produce, and the bakery’s signature brioche hot dogs, with Petrossian caviar served while supplies last. Part of every ticket supports Natoora’s Farm Fund, which provides grants to young farmers. Tickets are $78.

What I did last week.

Places or shows I went to over the last week. These are personal recommendations. If I had a cool week, they’ll be cool. If I didn’t, they won’t.

  1. Collective Retreats - While no one actually lives on Governors Island, you can spend the night there. Instead of a traditional afterparty following their wedding, my friends had everyone camp out together. "Camping" is a stretch though. Some of the tents are basically mini Airbnbs. They host yoga, rent bikes, have s'mores by the fire, and have restaurants on site. We did exactly none of those things, which means I'm already planning another weekend back. The views of Lower Manhattan are unmatched.

  2. The River Cafe - The wedding itself was at The River Café, finally helping me cross a longtime NYC bucket list item off. The space is so iconic and filled with flowers that it barely needs decorating. The food completely lived up to the reputation too. I think I ate an entire crispy duck through the passed appetizers before we even sat down. I understand why it’s one of the city’s most sought-after wedding venues.

  3. Il Leone - Despite being only a few minutes from me, I somehow hadn't been yet. It's definitely overpriced, but the pizzas were excellent and it has one of the best patios in Park Slope. I skipped the lobster pizza this time (market price scared me off), but I have a feeling I'll cave on my next visit.

  4. Wallace - Prospect Heights' new wine bar is exactly what Vanderbilt has been missing. I love how family-friendly the avenue is during the day, but it's nice to finally have somewhere open past 10 pm. It is still New York after all. It's a narrow space that's perfect for grabbing a seat at the bar, ordering a chilled red, and picking at a few small plates. I had an octopus and white bean salad that was really yummy.

  5. INA Consignment - had no idea INA had a Chelsea location. I walked in on the way to a gallery and unintentionally spent 40 minutes inside. When I hear ‘consignment’ I expect to have to dig for the good stuff. INA is the opposite. I found far too many pieces I wanted and spent my time trying to narrow them down. It's mostly designer, but there are plenty of genuinely good deals. If you want more vintage recommendations, check out the guide I put together with my favorites.
